openCanvasEvidence.claim: CanvasNodeMedia stores locator/source/asset/thumbnail/duration/size but no intrinsic width or height; image and video data store selected output identity separately from generation aspect and resolution.
openCanvasEvidence.boundary: Does not prove intrinsic dimensions are unavailable from the remote asset or DOM; only that the normalized graph descriptor omits them.

openCanvasEvidence.claim: Image upload probes decoded width/height, closes ImageBitmap or revokes the fallback object URL, chooses the closest supported generation aspect ratio and patches normalized image settings; video upload probes duration only.
openCanvasEvidence.boundary: The selected ratio is a model option, not retained exact intrinsic metadata.

openCanvasEvidence.claim: Image and video cards have fixed type widths and their media preview wrapper uses nodeData.aspectRatio, so request configuration rather than selected-media intrinsic dimensions drives preview height.
openCanvasEvidence.boundary: This is an upstream implementation choice, not LibTV source evidence.

openCanvasEvidence.claim: Canvas node previews, candidate grids and compact media controls use cover; the full-screen active image uses contain and its candidate thumbnails use cover.
openCanvasEvidence.boundary: Surface-role separation is reusable; exact fit/crop policy remains product-specific.

openCanvasEvidence.claim: Image/video history normalization clamps selected indexes, reconciles primary media with history and deduplicates by assetId or URL; output switching updates both selected index and primary media.
openCanvasEvidence.boundary: The normalized media entries still cannot reconcile per-output intrinsic aspect because they omit dimensions.

openCanvasEvidence.claim: Edited-image save appends and selects a new uploaded output but does not patch aspectRatio or store the exported canvas dimensions in CanvasNodeMedia.
openCanvasEvidence.boundary: A ratio mismatch is structurally possible; this audit did not execute an edited mixed-ratio save.

openCanvasEvidence.claim: The graph schema serializes optional node width/height while React Flow measured dimensions remain runtime-only; no NodeResizer, resize control or explicit resize callback exists in the fixed canvas source.
openCanvasEvidence.boundary: Serialized compatibility fields do not prove user-resize product semantics.

openCanvasEvidence.claim: Double-click centering and selected action/editor overlays resolve geometry through measured width/height, then node width/height, then fixed fallback values.
openCanvasEvidence.boundary: The method supports current-frame anchoring but does not solve stale measurement or define LibTV source offsets.

openCanvasEvidence.claim: Whole-canvas image drop repeats intrinsic-dimension ratio inference, whereas whole-canvas video drop stores duration and leaves the existing video aspect setting unchanged.
openCanvasEvidence.boundary: This is an image/video asymmetry, not a recommended LibTV policy.

openCanvasEvidence.claim: Node and thumbnail surfaces may render thumbnailUrl while the detail viewer uses the full media URL, but neither URL has independent dimensions or crop metadata in the normalized descriptor.
openCanvasEvidence.boundary: Does not prove current thumbnails have a different crop; it proves the descriptor cannot declare how to reconcile one.

observations.claim: No React Flow node resize/resizer selector was present in the observed current DOM.
observations.boundary: Current DOM absence does not prove the feature never appears for other node types or modes.

cloneFindings.claim: ImageNodeData width/height are displayed and handed to preview/edit owners, while React Flow node width/height independently control the node frame.
The ordinary ImageNode uses cover; ImagePreviewOverlay uses contain but trusts node-data dimensions instead of decoded intrinsic dimensions.
A newly added default image has 512x512 media data but a 512x288 graph frame, producing an undeclared center crop.
Most derived image actions inherit source media dimensions but use default image graph dimensions unless callers explicitly override them.
Director image capture stores actual/aspect metadata but always uses default landscape image node dimensions; portrait and square capture frames can therefore be cropped in the ordinary route.
Director animation export is a positive local method: graph node dimensions are aspect-aware and the actual video uses contain.
The same VideoNode type uses cover for poster-only ready state and contain for Director video playback, without a named rendition profile.

Picture-edit and subtitle-region coordinates normalize against the full node overlay; if the underlying poster is cover-cropped, the stored coordinates are visible-frame coordinates rather than declared intrinsic-media coordinates.
Image annotation sizes a blank backing canvas from the rendered node rect and does not declare a transform to intrinsic image space.
Ordinary image/video node data have no first-class output list, selected output identity, per-output dimensions or thumbnail/full rendition descriptor.
Generation settings are opaque display strings and cannot safely serve as a geometry authority.
The ordinary route uses React Flow measured width for selected video tools but has no explicit media-ready geometry epoch or output-switch remeasurement contract.
Shot Breakdown source/result surfaces force near-16:9 frames with cover regardless of declared source/result dimensions.
Initial shared-project clone fixtures align graph-frame ratios with their media labels, showing a useful source-shaped method that newer generic creation paths do not preserve.
